name: Valencia
title: Holidays in Valencia
intro: City beaches, a giant Gulliver to climb and the home of paella. Here's what Valencia is like, when to go and how long to stay.
image_alt: A sunny cathedral square with a fountain and a domed church
facts_note: The EU is bringing in new entry checks, so check the rules on GOV.UK before you book.
when_to_go: May, June and September are perfect, with warm sea and fewer crowds than midsummer. July and August are hot but the beach is right there. In mid-March the Fallas festival fills the streets with giant figures, fireworks and very loud firecrackers.

things.name: Oceanogràfic
things.blurb: Europe's biggest aquarium, with sharks, belugas and a dolphin show.

things.name: Turia Gardens
things.blurb: A park in an old riverbed, with bike paths and the giant Gulliver playground to climb.

things.name: City of Arts and Sciences
things.blurb: Futuristic buildings with a hands-on science museum and an IMAX cinema.

things.name: Malvarrosa Beach
things.blurb: A wide sandy city beach with a long promenade, a tram ride from the centre.

things.name: Bioparc
things.blurb: A zoo built like the African savannah, with no visible fences.

things.name: Albufera
things.blurb: Take a boat on the lagoon and eat paella where it was invented.

faqs.question: Is Valencia good for a family holiday?
faqs.answer: Yes. It's a city break and a beach holiday in one, it's flatter and calmer than Barcelona, and there's a lot for children.

faqs.question: How many nights do you need?
faqs.answer: Four nights covers the city, and a week lets you add plenty of beach days.

faqs.question: Do UK families need a visa?
faqs.answer: No, British passport holders can visit for up to 90 days in any 180 without a visa. New EU entry checks are being brought in, so check GOV.UK before you travel.

faqs.question: What is Fallas?
faqs.answer: A festival in mid-March when huge papier-mâché figures fill the streets, then get burned on the last night. It's spectacular but noisy and busy, and hotels book up early.
